title: Theori finds 5 critical NGINX vulnerabilities, urges immediate patching
text:
Theori finds 5 critical NGINX vulnerabilities, urges immediate patching - CHOSUNBIZ 
 2026년 11월 19일(목) Industry Finance Real Estate IT Retail Science Policy Society International Entertainment Culture Sports English IT Theori finds 5 critical NGINX vulnerabilities, urges immediate patching 
 AI helps uncover NGINX flaws that enable unauthenticated attacks 
 입력 2026.11.19. 10:04 조선비즈 구글 검색 먼저 보기 /Courtesy of Theori Inc. A critical security vulnerability has been found in "NGINX," web server software widely used by websites around the world, allowing external attackers to remotely execute malicious code without authentication.
 Theori Inc., an artificial intelligence (AI)-based cybersecurity company, said on the 19th that it had found 5 critical vulnerabilities in nginx that allow remote code execution (RCE) without authentication (CVE-2026-123007, CVE-2026-123634, CVE-2026-123633, CVE-2026-121810, CVE-2026-113425).
 NGINX is essential software that handles website and application requests and routes traffic. It is used in the infrastructure underpinning numerous companies and cloud services worldwide. According to global web technology research firm W3Techs, about 29.7% of websites worldwide whose web server software is known use NGINX.
 A Theori Inc. representative recommended urgent patching, saying, "Vulnerabilities found in this kind of software can affect the security of a wide range of internet services beyond individual websites."
 According to Theori Inc., the 5 vulnerabilities have different causes, but all allow attackers to execute arbitrary code on vulnerable NGINX servers without authentication. All 5 received a risk score of 9.2 out of 10 under the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS) 4.0 and were rated "Critical."
 In particular, when combined with a separately discovered Linux kernel vulnerability, the flaws could allow attackers to gain root privileges, potentially putting the entire server under their control.
 Of the 5 NGINX vulnerabilities identified, 4 were found autonomously without human intervention by "Xint," an AI-based autonomous security platform developed by Theori Inc. A Theori Inc. researcher found the remaining vulnerability. According to Theori Inc., Xint detected the major vulnerabilities in about 1 hour and 30 minutes, and researchers used the reproduction steps generated by the platform to complete a working proof-of-concept (PoC) exploit in about 10 minutes.
 Theori Inc. said it shared the vulnerabilities with F5, the developer of NGINX, and worked with major cloud providers, including Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft (MS) and Google, to coordinate security fixes and response measures.
 It also recommended that organizations using NGINX review the official security advisory, check affected versions and server configurations, and promptly apply relevant security updates and mitigation measures.
 "A vulnerability that allows code execution without authentication on a web server used around the world is the kind of discovery hackers regard as a holy grail," said Park Se-jun, CEO of Theori Inc. "This time, AI found most of them."
 "As AI gets faster at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities, it will become difficult for defenders to respond using only the traditional approach of having people analyze and check everything individually," Park said. "Combining AI's autonomous exploration capabilities with the validation expertise of security professionals will become even more important for security in the future."
